page.layout: One page of text in a single column. Running head at top, page number at top right. Two small notes in the right margin, beside the lines "Theodoberto" and "Hoc amictu". No left-margin notes that can be read. Catchword and signature at the foot.

main_text.p: piæ vitio laborantes, adeo furore væsanienti exstimulantur: ut ad vindictam converfæ,atrocia diræque faciinora conficiant: neque aliis, nec viris ipsis, nec filiis, nec sibi denique suoque pudori parcant. Sic nimirum THESSALICÆ quædam mulieres LAIDEM formosam meretriculam, quæ fui desiderio Græciam incenderat, quòd à Paufaniâ quodam Theffalo amaretur, ex invidiâ & zelotypiâ in fano Veneris ligneis fcabellis trucidaverunt: ut ex Timæi lib.15. hift. refert Athenæus lib.13.cap.10. Paufanias in Laconicis memorat, HELENAM post Menelai mortem, à Megapenthe & Nicostrato filiis Orefts fugatam, in Rhodum pervenisse: ubi cum POLYXENA Tlepolemi uxori, ad quam jure veteris amicitiæ diverterat, fufpecta effet: ab hujus ancillis, ipsius mandato, arbori fuspensa perierit. MEDEA à Jasone repudiata, cum ille nuptias celebraret cum Glaucâ Creontis Corinthiorum Regis filiâ, proprios libetos, ex Jasone quos susceperat, obtruncavit: sponsæ vero coronam, naphthâ illitam, misit: quam illa imprudens cum capiti impofuiffet: & propius ad ignes sacros, pro more sacrificatura, accessisset: à flammâ correpta, se simul & regiam totam, in quam confugerat, combusit. Hinc illud Virgilii Eclogâ 8.

p.i: Sævus amor docuit natorum sanguine matrem Commaculasse manus.

main_text.p: DEUTERIA Romana, Biterræ Dominâ, viduâ Theodoberto Austrasiæ & Mediomatricum Regi nupta; filiam formosissimam, ex priore viro susceptam, suspicata Theodobertum hujus amore captum, Viroduni submergi curavit: sicque leviffimæ suspicioni maternus amor cessit. Fulgosus lib.5.cap.8. XERXES Rex ab uxore AMESTRI donatus amiculo, quod ipsa texuerat, eo indutus, ad Artaxatam Masistris fratris filiam, & nurum suam, concesserat: cum quâ ubi se oblectavit, jussit à se petere, quodcunque vellet. Hoc amictu vox tandem multis precibus à Rege impetrato, Amestris non in puellam concepit odium, sed in illius matrem, quam hujus rei auctorem falsò credebat. Observa-sz. [?]349 [?]

page.notes: The top line of the first paragraph is partly worn; "piæ" and "vitio" are read from the scan with the ligature as printed. The numeral "lib.15." after "Timæi" is doubtful ("1ʃ" in print). The running head at the top is worn; "LIBROS IV" is a guess. The right-margin marks "sz." and "349" are unclear. The page number "401" is read from a worn top-right print. The verse lines are set in italic as one stanza. The left-margin marks are show-through and were left out.
